# Summary of Changes

Go ahead and update the `test_examples.py` file, doing so in such a way and to such a degree that it now goes on to properly include within itself the testing of the POST requests, and it does this specifically for the particular case of the "things_advanced" example that is there:
- One single successful POST request, which is the kind that is included here specifically in order to go and confirm as well as verify the correct and expected behavior of the example as it stands itself
- One invalid POST request, which is the kind that is included here specifically so as to properly and thoroughly test out the particular case of an empty body, one that happens to be paired up together with a non-zero `Content-Length` value that is found sitting right there inside of the header

Go ahead and update the `things_advanced.py` example itself as well, doing this specifically and deliberately in order to go and add `req.content_length` onto the `req.stream.read()` call that already sits there within it.

Go ahead and add one brand new entry over into the FAQ, and this is an entry which goes on to describe in detail the particular way and manner in which a person is able to go about customizing the various header values that end up being used for the express purpose of running the tests.

 you would get ``{'cookies': {'xxx': 'yyy', 'hello': 'world'}}``.
 
+How can I set header fields when simulating requests?
+-----------------------------------------------------
+
+Default header fields can be overwritten to simulate unexpected
+behavior. For instance, to test the condition where a ``POST``
+request has an empty body but the value of ``Content-Length``
+is non-zero, we can overwrite that value in the header.
+
+.. code:: python
+
+    import falcon
+    import falcon.testing
+    import pytest
+
+    class PostTest:
+
+        def on_post(self, req, resp):
+            if req.content_length in (None, 0):
+                resp.status = falcon.HTTP_200
+            else:
+                if req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0):
+                    resp.status = falcon.HTTP_201
+                else:
+                    resp.status = falcon.HTTP_400
+
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def client():
+        app = falcon.App()
+        app.add_route('/resource', PostTest())
+
+        return falcon.testing.TestClient(app)
+
+
+    def test_post_empty_body_with_length(client):
+        headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),]
+        body = ''
+        result = client.simulate_post(path='/resource', body=body, headers=headers)
+        assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)
+
